disclaimer.text: Indicative analysis — not auditor-grade evidence. Spectra runs 8 LLM agents over your code; findings are heuristic and require human verification before being treated as compliance evidence, audit input, or pass/fail signal in regulated workflows.

findings.title: Composition root carries excessive responsibility (god module)
findings.description: src/spectra/infrastructure/main.py is ~700 lines and owns: DI wiring, workspace allocation, ingest, preflight orchestration, source-file reading, token capping, policy enforcement, cache provisioning, cost tracker construction, audit wiring, receipt signing, JSON/SARIF rendering, classification redaction, secret logging, and CLI seam injection. While Clean Architecture intentionally concentrates wiring at the composition root, render-layer concerns (build_json_payload, _build_sarif, _redact_public_payload, _sarif_results) and pipeline stage logic (_ingest_workspace, _read_key_source_files, _apply_token_cap) are domain/adapter responsibilities that should not live alongside DI. This makes the file a change magnet and tightens coupling to nearly every other module.
findings.recommendation: Extract three modules: (1) spectra/infrastructure/report_serializers.py for build_json_payload/_build_sarif/_redact_public_payload; (2) spectra/use_cases/ingest_workspace.py for _ingest_workspace + _read_key_source_files + _apply_token_cap (these are pipeline phases, not wiring); (3) spectra/infrastructure/cache_wiring.py for _provision_cache/_resolve_cache_secret/_make_cache_key_factory. main.py should shrink to <250 lines containing only DI and the _run_analysis orchestrator.

findings.title: Adapter layer imports infrastructure (dependency rule violation)
findings.description: src/spectra/adapters/waiver_cli.py performs a deferred import of spectra.infrastructure.yaml_waiver_adapter inside waive_command (line ~regex 'from spectra.infrastructure.yaml_waiver_adapter import YamlWaiverAdapter'), and _get_signer() lazy-imports spectra.infrastructure.ed25519_signer. The module docstring explicitly acknowledges this ('Deferred import — break the adapters↔infrastructure circular at module load'). Per the stated Clean Architecture rule (adapters/ imports only entities/ and use_cases/), this is a Layer 3 → Layer 4 dependency, even when deferred. The lazy import only hides the cycle; it does not fix the dependency direction.
findings.recommendation: Move sign_waiver from YamlWaiverAdapter into a use-case-layer port (e.g., WaiverSignerPort in use_cases/interfaces.py) and have the composition root inject the concrete YamlWaiverAdapter at startup via a setter analogous to set_signer/set_keyring_backend. This removes the adapter→infrastructure import entirely and makes the seam consistent with the rest of the CLI controller's DI pattern.

findings.title: Adapter imports infrastructure module path inside cli_controller
findings.description: src/spectra/adapters/cli_controller.py's cli() function (lines ~end of analyze section) imports from spectra.infrastructure.audit_wiring, spectra.infrastructure.ed25519_signer, and spectra.infrastructure.receipt_signer directly. Although these are inside a function body (deferred), they cross the layer boundary in the wrong direction. The CLI adapter should receive these via setters from main.py only — it should never name infrastructure modules itself.
findings.recommendation: Remove the deferred infrastructure imports from cli(). The composition root (main.py) already injects _verifier, _shred_executor, _cache_provider, and _analyzer_factory; extend the same pattern by passing the Ed25519 signer adapter and verifier explicitly from main.cli() instead of having cli_controller.cli() reach into infrastructure. Move the signer/verifier wiring entirely into main.cli().

findings.title: _run_analysis function signature has 14 parameters
findings.description: _run_analysis in main.py accepts 14 parameters (repo_url, output_path, skip_critique, output_format, verbose, force, no_cache, agent_overrides, honor_gitignore, allow_secrets, audit_sink, classification, max_cost_usd, max_cost_per_hour). This signals that the CLI is plumbing every flag through one funnel without an intermediate Request value object. Adding a new flag requires touching three places: CLI command, factory signature, and _run_analysis.
findings.recommendation: Introduce an AnalysisInvocation frozen Pydantic model in entities/models.py that bundles all 14 fields, validated at the CLI boundary. _run_analysis then accepts a single invocation: AnalysisInvocation parameter. This shrinks the seam, allows adding fields without breaking call sites, and makes the analyzer_factory protocol stable.

findings.title: Path traversal validation susceptible to TOCTOU between symlink check and existence check
findings.description: In `_validate_local_path`, the symlink check uses `expanded.is_symlink()` and then `expanded.exists()`/`is_dir()` are called separately. This is a TOCTOU pattern (CWE-367) — between the symlink rejection and subsequent operations, the path could be replaced with a symlink. Additionally, only the root is checked for symlinks; intermediate path components could still be symlinks pointing outside intended areas. The `..` check uses `Path(raw).parts` which catches literal `..` segments but does not resolve the path first, so path normalization tricks (e.g. encoded variants) may bypass it. Mitigation: the validation runs at CLI boundary only and the GitAdapter is expected to perform its own validation.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the path with `Path(raw).expanduser().resolve(strict=True)` and compare against an allowed root, or use `os.path.realpath` and verify no component is a symlink. Combine the symlink/exists/is_dir checks via a single stat call to reduce TOCTOU window.

findings.title: Receipt signing failures silently degrade — verification status not surfaced
findings.description: `_attach_receipt` swallows a wide tuple of exceptions (OSError, ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, InvalidSignature, KeyringError) at DEBUG level only, returning the report without a receipt. Operators relying on receipts for tamper-evidence integrity (capability #57 / ADR-018) may not notice that receipts are missing across many runs. CWE-778: Insufficient Logging. The downgrade is intentional (ADR-018 §4: best-effort) but DEBUG-level logging will be invisible at default log levels.
findings.recommendation: Log receipt-signing failures at WARNING level (not DEBUG) so operators see the degradation in default logs. Optionally surface a `receipt_status` field on the report so consumers can detect missing-receipt runs without parsing logs.

findings.title: Cache HMAC secret resolution falls back silently on Windows (no geteuid)
findings.description: `_resolve_cache_secret` returns `None` when `os.geteuid` is unavailable (Windows), which disables the per-user HMAC binding on the cache (ADR-012). The cache adapter then operates without MAC verification. Although the comment notes 'per-user file isolation degraded; secret unavailable,' this means the integrity protection silently degrades on Windows installs without a clear operator warning at runtime. CWE-757: Selection of Less-Secure Algorithm During Negotiation.
findings.recommendation: On Windows, derive a per-user identifier from `os.getlogin()` or the SID and use that as the keyring `uid`, so HMAC enforcement is preserved. If degradation must remain, log at WARNING level (not silently) and surface the degraded state in `cache doctor`.

findings.title: Default zero-pad repo_signature in waive command weakens binding
findings.description: `waive_command` accepts `--repo-signature` defaulting to `"0" * 32` (32 zero hex chars). A waiver signed with a zero-padded signature is portable across repos but loses the repo-binding property — an attacker who steals a signed waiver could replay it against any repository. The comment says 'pin if known; default zero-pad for portability,' indicating intent, but the security trade-off is significant for a signing primitive. CWE-294: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay.
findings.recommendation: Default the repo_signature to the actual computed signature for the current workspace (resolve from `.git`/file tree) rather than zero-pad. If portable waivers are a use case, require an explicit `--portable` flag and warn the operator that the waiver will not be repo-bound.

findings.title: Receipt verification CLI accepts public-key path without integrity check
findings.description: `spectra verify` reads the public key via `_load_pub_pem` from either `--key` or the default path `~/.config/spectra/receipt.pub`. The file is read without any integrity check — an attacker who replaces the public-key file (e.g. via a writable home directory or supply-chain attack) can substitute their own key and have receipts they generated themselves verify as valid. CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity. Ed25519 signatures are only as trustworthy as the public-key distribution channel.
findings.recommendation: Document the public-key trust model clearly: receipts can only be trusted when the verifier obtains the public key out-of-band (e.g. from a signed git tag, a TUF metadata file, or an organization-distributed PEM with checksum). Consider supporting a `--key-fingerprint` argument that the operator must specify to bind the verification to a known fingerprint.

findings.title: Composition root function exceeds clean-architecture readability budget
findings.description: _run_analysis in src/spectra/infrastructure/main.py spans roughly lines 313-411 (~100 lines) and orchestrates 8+ helper calls inside a try/finally with multiple parameter pass-throughs. While the body is well-decomposed and each helper is small, the parameter-marshalling alone makes the function a single point of churn — every new pipeline argument touches the signature, the docstring, _assemble_context, and the helper call sites in lockstep.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a frozen RunOptions dataclass that bundles repo_url/output_path/skip_critique/format/cost-caps/etc. so _run_analysis takes (options) and forwards options.* to _assemble_context. Cuts the parameter list in half and isolates new flags to a single location.

findings.title: CLI analyze() command has very high parameter count and complexity
findings.description: analyze() in src/spectra/adapters/cli_controller.py declares ~30 typer.Option parameters covering 8 per-role model + 8 per-role effort flags, JSON overrides, cost caps, classification, audit, secrets, etc. The function then calls _validate_analyze_inputs, _gather_and_validate_overrides, _classification_filename, _print_run_header, asyncio.run wrapper, _handle_pipeline_exceptions, _print_summary, plus min-score and fail-on gates. PLR0913 is globally suppressed in pyproject.toml, hiding the ergonomic cost.
findings.recommendation: Group per-role model/effort flags behind a single --agent-config <role>=<model>:<effort> repeated option (or rely solely on --model-overrides JSON), keeping the global --model/--effort defaults. Reduces parameter surface by ~16 and makes future role additions table-driven.

findings.title: Per-file-ignores broadly disable assertion/typing/print/perf lints in tests
findings.description: pyproject.toml line 102 disables S101, ANN, PLR2004, PT011, T20, TC003, PERF401 across every tests/**/*.py file. While S101 (assert usage) is reasonable in tests, blanket disabling ANN (annotations) and PT011 (broad pytest.raises) lets test code drift in quality. Combined with [[tool.mypy.overrides]] disabling disallow_untyped_defs for tests, the test layer has materially weaker static checking than src/.
findings.recommendation: Keep S101 + ANN ignores but re-enable PT011 (require pytest.raises(SomeError, match=...) for clarity) and PERF401 in test fixtures. Document why the others are off in a comment so future contributors understand the trade-off.

findings.title: Broad except Exception in waive_command masks Pydantic vs other validation errors
findings.description: waive_command in waiver_cli.py catches ValueError specifically, then a fallback `except Exception as exc:` that always reports 'reason needs >=10 chars'. If a Pydantic validator other than reason fires (or a non-validation runtime error), the user sees a misleading message.
findings.recommendation: Catch pydantic.ValidationError explicitly and render its first error's loc + msg; let unrelated exceptions propagate. Add a test for a non-reason validation failure (e.g. malformed repo_signature) to lock in the behavior.

findings.title: build_verdict accepts object and uses getattr — duck-typing erodes type safety
findings.description: src/spectra/adapters/brand.py:build_verdict and src/spectra/adapters/analysis_presenter.py:_build_summary_text both type their report parameter as `object` and use getattr(...) with defaults to read score_card, findings, total_findings, etc. Given the strict mypy config (disallow_any_generics, strict=True), this is a deliberate type-safety escape hatch that bypasses checks for fields the rest of the codebase models with frozen Pydantic types.
findings.recommendation: Type these parameters as `AnalysisReport` (or a Protocol with the score_card/findings/repo_name attributes) and remove the getattr defaults. Use a real test double in tests instead of duck-typed objects.

findings.title: Public CLI command help text lacks usage examples
findings.description: `analyze`, `verify`, `cache shred`, `cache prune`, and `render pr-comment` Typer commands have one-line help strings but no usage examples in the docstring. Users running `spectra analyze --help` see only flag descriptions, not example invocations like `spectra analyze https://github.com/org/repo --quick --fail-on high`. The README/getting-started.md likely covers this, but inline help is the most-used reference surface.
findings.recommendation: Expand each `@app.command()` docstring with an `Examples:` section (Typer renders the full docstring in `--help`). Show a basic invocation, a CI-friendly invocation with `--fail-on` + `--no-cache`, and a cost-capped invocation. Same for `verify`, `cache *`, and `render pr-comment`.

findings.title: docs/error-codes.md anchor format coupled to GitHub auto-slug rules
findings.description: `_docs_link()` constructs URLs as `{_ERROR_DOCS_BASE}#{code.lower()}` for SPEC-001..SPEC-014. This relies on `docs/error-codes.md` having heading anchors that exactly match GitHub's auto-slug rules (lowercase, hyphens). If the doc uses a different heading style (e.g. `## SPEC-001: Git clone failed`), the slug becomes `#spec-001-git-clone-failed`, not `#spec-001`, and every CLI error message will produce a 404. No verification mechanism exists.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that loads `docs/error-codes.md`, extracts heading slugs, and asserts a slug matching exactly `spec-NNN` exists for every code in `ERRORS`. Alternatively use HTML anchors (`<a id="spec-001">`) in error-codes.md and document the contract in CONTRIBUTING.md.

findings.title: Hardcoded model lists duplicated across CLI, entities, and docstrings
findings.description: The allowed model identifiers (`claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-opus-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-haiku-4-5`) are defined in three places: `_ALLOWED_MODELS` in cli_controller.py, the `ModelId` Literal in entities/models.py, and inline in `_composite_model_versions()` in main.py. The cli_controller comment even acknowledges 'we duplicate the friendly allowed-list here only to fail fast'. Documentation must be kept in sync manually across all three; there is no documented contract for adding a new model.
findings.recommendation: Document the model-addition procedure in CONTRIBUTING.md as a checklist: (1) add to `ModelId` Literal in entities, (2) add to `_ALLOWED_MODELS` in cli_controller, (3) add to `_MODEL_COST` in entities/models.py for cost estimation, (4) update README pricing section. Better: derive `_ALLOWED_MODELS` from `typing.get_args(ModelId)` to eliminate one copy.

findings.title: Capability numbers (#6, #13, #17, #18, #56, #57) referenced without an index
findings.description: Code comments throughout `main.py`, `cli_controller.py`, and `models.py` reference 'Capability #56', '#57', '#17', '#18', '#13', '#6', 'Q2 #19', 'Q2 #20', 'Roadmap #13', 'Fix R3-Arch-3', etc. None of the visible documentation files (README, CLAUDE.md, glossary, getting-started) are confirmed to contain a capability index. A reader cannot resolve `#56` → 'classification-aware report redaction' without grepping source. This is bus-factor risk.
findings.recommendation: Add a `docs/capabilities.md` (or a section in `docs/glossary.md`) mapping every `#N` capability and `Q2 #N` reference to a one-line description and the ADR(s) that govern it. Same for `Fix R3-Arch-N` codes. Cross-link from CLAUDE.md so contributors landing in source comments can resolve the numbers.

findings.title: Disclaimer URL points at README anchor that may not exist
findings.description: `DISCLAIMER_URL = "https://github.com/leocder07/spectra#disclaimer"` is hardcoded in `entities/disclaimer.py` and surfaces in every JSON, HTML, and SARIF report. If `README.md` does not contain a heading that auto-slugs to `#disclaimer`, every consumer following the link gets a 404. Also: the URL is hardcoded to a specific GitHub fork (`leocder07/spectra`) which couples user-facing reports to one maintainer's account.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that fetches `README.md` and asserts a `## Disclaimer` (or equivalent) heading exists. Consider making `DISCLAIMER_URL` configurable via env var or pyproject so forks can rebrand without patching source. Document the contract in CONTRIBUTING.md.

findings.title: Dependency on unmaintained pysqlcipher3 package
findings.description: pyproject.toml pins pysqlcipher3>=1.2,<2.0. The pysqlcipher3 package on PyPI has been unmaintained for years (last meaningful release in 2020) and does not provide modern Python wheels. The maintainer has explicitly recommended migrating to actively-maintained alternatives like sqlcipher3-binary or sqlcipher3-wheels. Bundling an unmaintained crypto-adjacent dependency in a security-oriented tool is a notable supply-chain risk, and the comment in pyproject.toml acknowledges Windows wheel scarcity which stems from this lack of maintenance.
findings.recommendation: Switch to sqlcipher3-binary (active fork with prebuilt wheels) or sqlcipher3-wheels. The adapter already degrades to plain SQLite on import failure, so the migration is low-risk: replace the package, retest the SqliteCacheAdapter fallback path on Windows + Linux + macOS, and update ADR-012.

findings.title: Lockfile referenced in PLAN is missing from provided artifacts
findings.description: The PLAN identifies requirements.lock as a focus file, but no lockfile contents were supplied for review. Without a committed lockfile (or pip-compile/uv-lock output) reproducible builds and SBOM generation cannot be verified. The pyproject.toml uses range pins (>=X,<Y) on every dependency, so transitive resolution is non-deterministic across CI runs unless a lockfile is enforced.
findings.recommendation: Confirm requirements.lock is generated from pyproject.toml via pip-compile (pip-tools) or uv lock, committed to the repo, and consumed by both ci.yml and publish.yml via `pip install -r requirements.lock`. Add a CI step that fails if the lockfile drifts from pyproject.toml. Generate an SBOM (CycloneDX) from the lockfile during release.

findings.title: GitHub Actions workflows and action.yml not provided for review
findings.description: The PLAN flags .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/publish.yml, and action.yml as supply-chain surfaces (publish workflow + GitHub Action distribution), but none of these files were included in the source code. CI/CD supply-chain hygiene (action SHA pinning vs tag refs, OIDC trusted publishing to PyPI, permissions: contents: read minimization, dependency review) cannot be assessed without the workflow contents.
findings.recommendation: Verify that publish.yml uses PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC) rather than long-lived API tokens, pins every third-party action to a 40-char commit SHA (not a moving tag), declares minimal `permissions:` per job, and runs `pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.lock`. Verify action.yml does not download untrusted scripts at runtime.

findings.title: Unbounded asyncio.gather for source file reads can spike thread pool
findings.description: _gather_source_reads dispatches up to MAX_HEURISTIC_FILES concurrent read_file calls via asyncio.gather, each likely offloaded to the default thread pool executor. With MAX_HEURISTIC_FILES=20 this is fine, but if the cap is raised the default thread pool (min(32, os.cpu_count()+4)) becomes a bottleneck and may starve other async I/O sharing the loop.
findings.recommendation: Add an asyncio.Semaphore (e.g. limit 8-16) around the read_file calls so concurrency is bounded by an explicit policy independent of MAX_HEURISTIC_FILES. This also keeps the default thread pool free for git/cache I/O.

cross_cutting_insights: arch-005 and qual-001 describe the same root cause (parameter sprawl through the composition root); a single AnalysisInvocation/RunOptions value object resolves both.

arch-001 and arch-002 are the same structural defect (adapters→infrastructure deferred imports) in two files; fix as one refactor by moving signer/verifier injection fully into main.cli() via setters.

qual-007, qual-010, and doc-011 all touch the bare-except / lazy-import patterns in waiver_cli/cli_controller. Resolving arch-001/arch-002 (proper DI) eliminates the lazy imports and the misleading exception handlers in one pass.

sec-002 (DEBUG-only receipt failure logging), sec-006 (silent Windows HMAC degradation), and sec-009 (unverified public-key trust) form a 'silent security degradation' theme — operators cannot observe when integrity guarantees weaken. A unified 'security_status' field on reports plus WARNING-level logging would address all three.

doc-006 (model list duplicated in 3 places) and doc-007 (capability numbers without an index) both indicate the project is outgrowing ad-hoc cross-referencing; a single 'contracts' page (models, capabilities, ADR map, error codes) would consolidate doc-005, doc-006, doc-007.

dep-000 (unmaintained pysqlcipher3) compounds with sec-006 (Windows HMAC degradation) — both weaken the cache integrity story on Windows specifically; migrating to sqlcipher3-binary may also enable consistent cross-platform HMAC behavior.
